sections.title: Predictive analytics that stays accurate and trusted

blocks.heading: Data readiness drives cost
paragraphs: Unlike some AI categories, predictive analytics cost depends mostly on the quality, completeness and accessibility of your historical data. We assess it first so the estimate reflects reality.

blocks.heading: Drift monitoring is standard
paragraphs: When distribution shift or accuracy degradation exceeds a threshold, monitoring alerts your team for retraining. We build this into every system rather than selling it as an add-on.

blocks.heading: Explainability where it is required
paragraphs: Regulated contexts such as credit, employment and clinical decisions require individual-level explanations; we integrate SHAP as standard for these use cases.

sections.title: Predictive analytics pricing reference
sections.note: Ranges reflect ClickMasters' fixed-price project fees. Retraining, serving and monitoring costs are separate and modeled during discovery.

items.question: How much does predictive analytics development cost?
items.answer: $30,000–$300,000. The most common enterprise projects — churn prediction, demand forecasting, fraud detection and lead scoring — typically run $35,000–$100,000.

items.question: How much historical data do we need?
items.answer: It depends on the prediction target. Churn models typically need 12–24 months of history with several hundred churned examples; fraud models need enough historical fraud cases to learn rare events — typically 1,000+ labeled instances.

items.question: Is $30,000 enough for a useful system?
items.answer: For a focused single use case such as lead scoring or basic churn with accessible, relatively clean data: yes. For regulated applications (credit, clinical) or complex multi-variable forecasting, budget $50,000–$100,000.

items.question: How accurate can predictive analytics be?
items.answer: AUC-ROC of 0.75–0.90 is typical for well-built churn and lead scoring models with adequate data. We validate accuracy on your specific data before deployment.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: 10–36 weeks depending on scope. A single use case with accessible data takes 10–18 weeks; a multi-model platform with compliance documentation takes 18–36 weeks.

items.question: What happens when predictions start to degrade?
items.answer: Drift monitoring detects distribution shift or accuracy degradation beyond a threshold and alerts for retraining. It is built in as standard.

sections.heading: Turn your historical data into forward-looking decisions
sections.text: Tell us which outcome you want to predict and what data you hold. An engineer will reply within one business day with a data readiness view and budget range.
